pathway.title: Xerox Holdings Corp — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Business risk is weak because a mostly recurring revenue base is shrinking. Post sale revenue was 79% of FY2025 revenue and committed multi-year service obligations were USD 636 million at 2026-09-30, but on a pro forma basis revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in the first nine months of 2026, and the IT Solutions line fell 12.1%. Equipment installations rose 9.0% in the third quarter of 2026 and the pro forma decline narrowed from the second quarter, which is a first sign of stabilisation rather than a trend. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 59, 62, 66

Leverage is high and has fallen only because earnings recovered, not because debt fell. Net debt of USD 3,808 million at 2026-09-30 is USD 3,754 million pro forma for the exchange of 2028 notes expected on 2026-11-13, and pro forma net leverage is not established. Net debt is 4.46x house-adjusted EBITDA of USD 854 million for the last twelve months against 6.42x at FY2025, a fall of 1.96x in which net debt rose USD 73 million and EBITDA rose 46.74%. Reported EBITDA is negative USD 275 million for the same twelve months after the USD 959 million goodwill impairment, the issuer states no EBITDA, and its own target of total debt below 3.0x EBITDA compares with 4.94x on the house measure. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C7; calculation C19

Interest absorbs a growing share of earnings, so coverage is thin and falling. Adjusted operating income plus depreciation covered non-financing interest expense 2.18x over the last twelve months against 4.23x in FY2024, because non-financing interest expense rose 64.88% in the first nine months of 2026 and total interest expense rose 41.45%, on higher rates on the Lexmark borrowings and the brand financing, and the 2025 secured issues carry coupons of 10.25% and 13.5%. The 13.00% notes due 2030 step up toward 16.75% by July 2030, and reported EBITDA covered FY2025 cash interest only 0.65x; cash interest is not printed for the 2026 interim periods. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96, 219–220, 227; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C18; calculation C14

Cash generation is the weakest dimension. Net cash used in operating activities was USD 77 million in the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow for the last twelve months was USD 37 million, or 4.33% of house-adjusted EBITDA against 76.68% in FY2024, and management cut its 2026 operating cash flow guidance to USD 145 million to USD 195 million from about USD 340 million on lower profitability, lower proceeds from sales of finance receivables and lower collections of tariff refunds. The range needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter against USD 208 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and a repeat of last year's quarter would leave the year at USD 131 million, below the range. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

Liquidity is adequate to the end of 2027 but the refinancing wall behind it is large. Cash of USD 412 million and net ABL availability of about USD 225 million cover the USD 217 million of principal due to the end of 2027 by 2.94x, and management says liquidity is sufficient for at least twelve months, but principal due is USD 752 million in 2028, USD 1,137 million in 2029 and USD 1,042 million in 2030, USD 2,931 million in all, and the ABL matures in May 2028. Pro forma cash for the exchange is not established, because accrued interest on the exchanged notes is paid in cash and not stated. Management expects to address the maturities through cash from operations, refinancings and liability management whose timing and terms are uncertain. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 56, 95, 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C12

Creditors are increasingly ranked by security and by entity, which raises class-specific risk for unsecured holders. About 47.15% of principal debt is now secured, USD 451 million sits in subsidiaries below Xerox Corporation, USD 450 million of it the brand financing, and the exchange would add about USD 120 million of first lien notes, while management states that further transactions may be pari passu with or effectively senior to existing debt. The company's own estimate puts the fair value of Holdings long-term debt at 49.10% of carrying amount against 76.02% for Xerox Corporation, which is an estimate and not a traded price. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47, 56, 98–99, 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 216–217; calculation C9; calculation C8

Financial policy is moving toward creditors but equity no longer protects them, and governance risk is medium. Dividends on common and preferred stock are suspended from January 2027, USD 200 million of notes were bought back at 50.50% of principal and capital expenditure is 1.23% of revenue, yet Holdings reports a shareholders' deficit of USD 683 million and ownership, board and related-party disclosure sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 40, 56; calculation C11; calculation C17

blocks.title: Company and operating model
columns: Why it matters to a creditor

cells.text: Management describes Xerox as a workplace technology company building services-led, software-enabled workplace solutions. Print and Other designs, develops and sells document systems, supplies, services and related financing; IT Solutions sells integrated IT infrastructure, managed IT, network, security and cloud services
Cash comes from equipment placements, recurring supplies and service, financing income and IT resale, which differ in margin and cyclicality
Revenue 7,022: equipment sales 1,488 (21%) and post sale revenue 5,534 (79%); Print and Other 6,272 (89%) and IT Solutions 761 (11%) before an elimination of 11
Post sale revenue gives visibility, but it follows an installed base that is shrinking
Revenue 5,636: equipment sales 1,158 (21%), post sale revenue 3,955 (70%) and IT Solutions 523 (9%); Print and Other 5,113 (91%)
Lexmark lifts reported growth to 12.9%, so pro forma growth of -5.0% is the better read of the business
Pro forma revenue change -7.6% in FY2025 and -5.0% in nine months 2026; third quarter 2026 revenue 1,868, down 4.7%, or 5.8% before a licensing agreement benefit of 1.1 percentage points
Debt is sized on a revenue base that is still falling by mid single digits
Adjusted operating income 302 in FY2024 and 248 in FY2025; nine months 2026 399 against 146 reported and 243 pro forma; nine months segment profit Print and Other 443, IT Solutions 21, corporate -65
The recovery is cost-led, and IT Solutions earns little (21 on revenue of 537)

Customers range from small businesses to Fortune 1000 companies, governments, schools and print companies; management says the business does not depend on a single customer or a few customers; sales are direct, including a new inside sales team, and through distributors, dealers, resellers and integrators; leases are financed through XFS

No concentration is disclosed; committed multi-year service obligations of 636 at 2026-09-30 (644 at 2025-12-31) are recognized over one to five years, renewal rates are not disclosed, and early termination penalties may not fully cover the investment in service contracts

FY2025 revenue by location of the reporting subsidiary: United States 3,985, Europe 1,952, Canada 464, Latin America 274, Asia Pacific 154, other 193; about 43% of revenue is outside the United States
Foreign currency and cash held abroad affect how much cash reaches the parent that issues most unsecured debt

Largest sites are Webster, New York and Juarez, Mexico; FUJIFILM Business Innovation is the largest strategic sourcing partner, with purchases of 811 in 2025, 886 in 2024 and 933 in 2023; management says a material portion of manufacturing is outsourced
Supplier terms drive gross margin; purchases were 11.55% of FY2025 revenue

Finance assets 1,701 at 2025-12-31 and 1,481 at 2026-09-30 (receivables 1,209, lease equipment 272); assumed 7:1 debt to equity gives financing debt of 1,296 of total debt of 4,220 and core debt of 2,924; receivable sales to funding partners raised 1,102 in 2023, 752 in 2024 and 357 in 2025, and 214 and 122 in nine months 2025 and 2026
The finance perimeter is funded by secured debt and receivable sales; falling sales cut operating cash flow and can trigger first lien prepayments
Print and Other has lower revenue, operating profit and cash flow in the first and third quarters; IT Solutions is stronger in the second and third quarters
Liquidity is tightest in the first quarter and third quarter operating cash flow is weak for print

About 22,900 employees at 2025-12-31, up 36.3% on Lexmark; about 15% are in unions or works councils; run-rate gross savings above 500 through 2025; a workforce reduction was announced in October 2025; synergy target above 300 by the end of 2027
Restructuring cash costs (60 paid in nine months 2026) compete with debt service

The Xerox brand trademarks and related intellectual property were contributed on 2026-02-17 to XRX Brandco Holdings LLC and are licensed back to Xerox Corporation and chosen subsidiaries for a royalty of 2.0% of specified revenue; the licence has a 10-year initial term with five-year automatic renewals, either party may end it at term end on 18 months' notice, and the joint venture may end it on certain defaults by Holdings, including insolvency or change of control, with a 90-day sell-off period for inventory; Xerox held 4,153 United States patents and 159 trademarks at 2025-12-31
The right to trade under the Xerox brand now rests on a licence from a financing vehicle

Management Language: Xerox believes it is the leader, or among the leaders, in entry, mid-range and high-end print; larger print competitors are Brother, Canon, FUJIFILM Business Innovation, HP, Konica Minolta, Kyocera and Ricoh
No market share data are in the supplied filings, and one named competitor is also the largest sourcing partner

runs.text: The first strength is a recurring, geographically diversified revenue base with no stated customer concentration, because post sale revenue is 79% of FY2025 revenue and committed obligations are USD 636 million, which gives cash flow visibility that supports debt service through 2027. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19

The second strength is a cost-led earnings recovery, because adjusted operating income rose to USD 399 million from USD 243 million pro forma and the issuer targets more than USD 300 million of synergies by the end of 2027, which lowers leverage if it is delivered. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C20

The third strength is liquidity and financial policy that protect the next two years, because cash of USD 412 million and net ABL availability of about USD 225 million cover principal due to the end of 2027 by 2.94x, dividends are suspended and debt was bought back at 50.50% of principal; pro forma cash for the exchange of 2028 notes expected on 2026-11-13 is not established. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 42, 56; calculation C12

The fourth strength is low capital intensity at 1.23% of revenue, which keeps capital spending from consuming cash, although it also leaves little room to cut. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation C11

The first weakness is a shrinking base, because pro forma revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in nine months 2026, which reduces the cash flow before interest that supports the debt. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 62

The second weakness is weak cash generation, because operating cash flow was negative USD 77 million in nine months 2026 and free cash flow was 4.33% of house-adjusted EBITDA, which leaves refinancing and asset-backed funding to meet maturities. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 97; calculation C4

The third weakness is a thin and falling interest cover of 2.18x on adjusted operating income plus depreciation, because higher rates on acquisition borrowings and the brand financing raised non-financing interest expense by 64.88% in nine months 2026. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C2; calculation C3

The fourth weakness is a maturity wall and eroding priority, because USD 2,931 million falls due in 2028 to 2030, 47.15% of principal debt is secured and the exchange and brand financing move claims ahead of unsecured notes, which raises class-specific risk. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 99–101; calculation C1; calculation C9

The fifth weakness is negative equity and unsettled governance, because Holdings reports a deficit of USD 683 million and ownership and board disclosure is not supplied, which removes a book cushion and leaves sponsor support unassessable. Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: Two acquisitions explain most of the change in the structure since 2024. ITsavvy, bought on 2024-11-20, created the IT Solutions segment for USD 404 million, of which USD 194 million was cash and USD 210 million was seller notes due in October 2025 and January 2026. Lexmark, bought from Ninestar Group Company Limited on 2025-07-01, cost USD 768 million at closing including USD 93 million of cash acquired, and USD 749 million after a USD 19 million working capital adjustment finalized in the first quarter of 2026. The 2024 annual report described the pending Lexmark deal as USD 1.5 billion inclusive of net debt and other assumed liabilities, and the bridge from that figure to the equity price is not itemised. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 190–194; 10-K_2024-12-31_xrx-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 183; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C3; calculation C4

New debt followed the same path. In March 2024 Holdings issued USD 500 million of notes due 2029 and USD 400 million of 3.75% convertible notes due 2030. In April and May 2025 Xerox Corporation issued USD 400 million of 10.25% first lien notes due 2030 at 99% of par and USD 500 million of 13.5% second lien notes due 2031 at 98% and 95% of par, and about USD 494 million of escrowed second lien proceeds was released at the Lexmark closing. On 2025-07-01 Holdings issued USD 125 million of 13.00% unsecured notes due June 2026 and USD 250 million of 13.00% notes due 2030 with a pre-funded warrant, and Xerox Corporation borrowed USD 327 million of incremental first lien term loans. In 2025 Xerox received about USD 375 million from issuing senior notes and about USD 904 million from secured debt. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-31_xrx-20241231.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 124, 218–222

The February 2026 joint venture is the largest new financing since the 2025 annual report. Xerox Corporation contributed the Xerox brand trademarks and related intellectual property to XRX Brandco Holdings LLC for Class B units, and investors funded USD 405 million of five-year senior secured term loans and USD 45 million of Class A units, which carry a mandatory cumulative redemption in five years unless the holders defer it. The proceeds were distributed to Xerox Corporation for general corporate purposes and for opportunistic work on the capital structure, including debt repayment. The 2025 annual report states USD 42 million of fees, while the third quarter report states USD 46 million paid at closing and USD 8 million later. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 262–263; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12, 39; calculation C8

Equity-linked and liability management steps followed in 2026. Holders of common stock, Series A preferred stock and the convertible notes received warrants to buy shares at USD 8.00 each for cash or with designated notes, over a number of shares equal to 58.01% of those outstanding, and 1.36% of the warrants had been exercised by 2026-09-30, one exercise retiring about USD 8 million of the convertible notes. The company also repurchased USD 194 million of the 2028 notes and USD 6 million of the 2031 second lien notes, and sold rights to USD 105 million of tariff refund receivables for about USD 80 million of cash, a discount of USD 25 million, which is shown in financing activities with a USD 81 million liability outside total debt at 2026-09-30. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 261; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 40–41, 49; calculation C23; calculation C24; calculation C14; calculation C29

Two announced steps are not yet complete. An exchange of about USD 174 million of 2028 notes for about USD 120 million of new first lien notes of Xerox Corporation and shares equal to 2.93% of those outstanding was expected to close on or about 2026-11-13, and the board suspended common and preferred dividends from January 2027, with the preferred dividend continuing to accumulate. No supplied document confirms the exchange closed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 56; calculation C18; calculation C19

fields.value: Financial foundation for Xerox Holdings Corp (issuer xrx-1770450), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's financial statements, debt, liquidity and credit metrics from the five supplied filings, on the Xerox Holdings Corporation consolidated perimeter.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Reported EBITDA is negative for the twelve months to 30 September 2026 after a goodwill impairment, and net debt is 4.46x house-adjusted EBITDA, so creditors rely on cash flow that was negative for nine months. House-adjusted EBITDA of USD 854 million is the issuer's adjusted operating income plus depreciation and equipment financing interest, an analyst measure, because the issuer states no EBITDA.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–6, 21, 24; calculation C55; calculation C56; calculation C58

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash of USD 412 million and net ABL availability of about USD 225 million exceed the USD 217 million of principal due to the end of 2027, but USD 752 million falls due in 2028 and needs refinancing. Management expects full-year operating cash flow of USD 145 million to USD 195 million, which needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter, and an exchange of 2028 notes expected to close on 2026-11-13 is not confirmed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 42, 56, 95, 97, 100–101; calculation C41; calculation C39; calculation C40

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Subsequent events are flagged with their dates and kept out of the period figures: an exchange of Holdings 5.50% notes due 2028 expected to close on or about 2026-11-13, and the suspension of common and preferred dividend payments from January 2027, both stated in October 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The register is drawn at 2025-12-31, the latest date for which any filing prints each instrument, because the 2026 quarterly reports print debt only by obligor. The Reporting Currency Amount column of the twelve drawn instruments (principal, USD millions) is 4,344; with the Financing cost adjustment of -97 it equals Total Debt of 4,247 at 2025-12-31. Changes in 2026 are the repurchase of USD 194 million of the 5.50% notes due 2028 and USD 6 million of the second lien notes, the USD 8 million extinguished on warrant exercise of the convertible notes, the joint venture term loans and Class A Units of about USD 450 million and ABL borrowings of USD 75 million at 2026-11-05.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ratios use derived reported EBITDA, which is negative or distorted by the goodwill impairments, so house-adjusted leverage in the calculation register is the more informative reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cover is available only for full years because the 2026 quarterly reports print no interest paid.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Undrawn facilities are the ABL's net availability at filing dates, limited by the borrowing base, not commitments of USD 425 million.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The ladder is principal by period at 2026-09-30, not carrying value, and it includes the joint venture term loans and Class A Units.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The EBITDA shown is house-adjusted, an analyst measure that excludes goodwill impairment, restructuring and other one-time items, while reported EBITDA is negative for FY2024 and the LTM.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The stack is drawn at 2025-12-31 and leaves out the 110 secured promissory note, the 3 of secured borrowings and the undrawn ABL because their rank or drawn amount is not stated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer states no adjusted EBITDA, so no bridge can be drawn from the method's definition.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer states no EBITDA, so the reported measure is derived from the statements and it absorbs the third-quarter 2026 goodwill impairment of USD 959 million, which leaves EBITDA for the twelve months to 30 September 2026 at negative USD 275 million and total debt over EBITDA not calculable, as it is for FY2024, when a USD 1,058 million impairment had the same effect. At FY2025, with no impairment, reported EBITDA of USD 177 million gives total debt of 23.99x and cover of 0.65x on the USD 272 million of cash interest paid, which shows how little earnings stood behind the debt before Lexmark contributed for a full year.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Source readiness (CP-0); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 150, 152, 227; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; calculation C55; calculation C64

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the house-adjusted measure, net debt is 4.46x LTM EBITDA against 6.42x at FY2025 and 4.64x at FY2024, and total debt is 4.94x against 7.30x at FY2025. The improvement is earnings, not repayment: net debt rose by USD 73 million from 2025-12-31 to 2026-09-30, while adjusted operating income for the nine months was USD 399 million against USD 146 million a year earlier, a rise of USD 253 million, which the issuer attributes to integration synergies and cost discipline, although revenue fell 4.7% in the third quarter of 2026 against a third quarter 2025 that already included Lexmark, so the gain is cost-led.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 151, 187; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4, 21, 59, 66; calculation C58; calculation C60; calculation C62; calculation C59; calculation C61; calculation C65; calculation C67

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The house measure is generous in two ways. It excludes restructuring charges and the non-service cost of retirement plans, although the company paid USD 60 million for restructuring and contributed USD 118 million to retirement plans in the first nine months of 2026, and it adds back equipment financing interest so that it matches total debt that includes USD 1,296 million of financing debt supporting finance receivables and operating lease equipment. Against core debt of USD 2,924 million, the ratio to adjusted operating income plus depreciation is 3.75x, against 5.56x at FY2025, whose earnings held Lexmark for only six months.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is the recovery in adjusted operating income and the issuer's own targets: it states run-rate synergies above USD 300 million by the end of 2027, and the October 2026 exchange would cut principal by up to about USD 54 million while moving about USD 120 million of maturities from 2028 to 2030. That view would win if operating cash flow converts: management's range for 2026 needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter, against USD 208 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and a shortfall would leave interest, restructuring and the 2028 maturities to be funded from cash and the ABL.

Severity: Low. Action: obtain any segment cash flow disclosure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance for Xerox Holdings Corp (issuer xrx-1770450), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the issuer's business, ownership and corporate structure, transactions and new debt, and governance and shareholder behaviour, drawn from the five supplied filings. The source readiness findings set the limits of what the filings can support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors rely on a shrinking print business with no identified controlling shareholder, two debt-funded acquisitions, negative book equity and a brand now held in a joint venture whose lenders have first call on it, so structure and priority matter most.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 84; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 9–12; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 190–194; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 269, 271; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C8; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management's capital allocation has moved toward creditors: common dividends declared fell 81.51% from 2023 to 2025 and are suspended from January 2027, and 2026 repurchases retired about USD 200 million of notes for about USD 101 million. The 2023 buyback of about USD 542 million of shares from one holder group was debt-funded, ownership is not established, and governance risk is medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 126, 254; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 56; calculation C12; calculation C14; calculation C7

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Recurring post sale revenue gives the business cash visibility, but the installed base is shrinking and the 2026 recovery is cost-led. Post sale revenue was 79% of FY2025 revenue and equipment sales 21%, management says the business does not depend on a single customer or a few customers, and about 43% of revenue is earned outside the United States. Committed multi-year service obligations were USD 636 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 644 million at 2025-12-31, which is small beside post sale revenue because most service revenue is invoiced as rendered. On a pro forma basis that treats the acquired businesses as owned throughout, revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in the first nine months of 2026, while adjusted operating income rose to USD 399 million from USD 243 million, which the issuer attributes to integration synergies and cost discipline. A licensing agreement added 1.1 percentage points to third quarter 2026 revenue, so the decline before it was 5.8% rather than 4.7%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 84; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 59, 62, 66–67, 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 183; calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C27; calculation C13; calculation C28

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Growth has been bought with secured and high-coupon debt, so the two acquisitions add to creditor risk until the synergies are proven. ITsavvy cost USD 404 million in November 2024, of which USD 210 million was seller notes at fair value. Lexmark cost USD 768 million for the equity at closing in July 2025, against a headline of USD 1.5 billion that included net debt and other assumed liabilities, and USD 749 million after the working capital adjustment, and was financed alongside USD 500 million of 13.5% second lien notes and USD 250 million of 13.00% senior notes due 2030 whose coupon steps up to 16.75% by July 2030, while USD 327 million of incremental first lien term loans refinanced USD 323 million of Lexmark's own debt. Lexmark contributed USD 962 million of 2025 revenue, 13.70% of the total, and a net loss of USD 119 million. The synergy target has risen from more than USD 200 million within two years to more than USD 300 million by the end of 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 190–194, 218–222; 10-K_2024-12-31_xrx-20241231.htm.jsonl, pages 7–8, 183; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation C3; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Shareholder distributions have been cut hard, which supports creditors, but the preferred stock keeps accruing and the last large distribution was debt-funded. Common dividends declared were USD 146 million in 2023, USD 128 million in 2024 and USD 27 million in 2025, after the annual dividend was cut from USD 1.00 to USD 0.50 per share in the first quarter of 2025 and to USD 0.10 in the second. The suspension from January 2027 is expected to conserve about USD 28 million a year, yet the Series A preferred stock, with a liquidation value of USD 180 million and a cumulative 8% dividend of USD 14 million a year, continues to accumulate dividends during the suspension. In September 2023 the company bought about USD 542 million of its shares from Carl C. Icahn and affiliates at USD 15.84 per share, funded by a USD 555 million loan that was refinanced with the USD 550 million Term Loan B.

fields.name: Quote

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The Xerox brand and related intellectual property now sit in a joint venture financed ahead of the other creditors, which is the largest change to the structure since the acquisitions. In February 2026 funds managed by Angelo, Gordon & Co. (together called TPG) and other investors lent USD 405 million of five-year senior secured term loans and bought USD 45 million of Class A units of XRX Brandco Holdings LLC, about USD 450 million in all, with the term loans secured on substantially all assets of the entity and its subsidiary, including the contributed intellectual property. Xerox Corporation consolidates the entity, and the royalty of 2.0% of specified revenue that the licensees pay it is held in a reserve account for the lenders, with certain subsidiaries of Holdings guaranteeing and securing the licence obligations. The joint venture can end the licence on certain defaults by Holdings, including insolvency or a change of control, after which the licensees keep only a 90-day sell-off period for inventory, so a default would put the use of the brand itself at stake. The term loans cost more than 11% a year even at the reference rate floor and the instruments amortize USD 81 million a year from the fourth quarter of 2026, and 10.37% of principal debt now sits in subsidiaries below Xerox Corporation, almost all of it in this joint venture. Whether the contributed assets had been collateral for the existing first and second lien notes is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Book equity has gone, so reported numbers no longer show any loss-absorbing layer beneath the debt. After the USD 959 million goodwill impairment on the Print and Other reporting unit in the third quarter of 2026, Holdings reports a shareholders' deficit of USD 683 million against equity of USD 444 million at 2025-12-31, Xerox Corporation reports a deficit of USD 492 million, and USD 897 million of goodwill remains on that unit. The issuer warns that future impairments may be possible if forecasts weaken further.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership and control are not established, so shareholder willingness cannot be assessed and the medium governance risk rests on issuer behaviour alone. The annual report places beneficial ownership, directors, compensation and related-party items in a proxy statement that is not supplied, no controlling holder or financial sponsor is named, and the holder of the Series A preferred stock is not named. Four of the six executive officers took their present roles in 2025, including a chief financial officer who joined with Lexmark. Reporting is audited with effective internal control, but Lexmark was left out of the 2025 internal control audit, representing 13% of assets and 14% of revenue, and its purchase accounting needed corrections in both the fourth quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liability management is selective across note series and holders, which raises class-specific risk for unsecured noteholders. In 2026 the company repurchased USD 194 million of its 5.50% notes due 2028 and USD 6 million of its 13.5% second lien notes due 2031 for about USD 101 million, 50.50% of principal, and booked a USD 95 million gain over nine months. In October 2026 it agreed with certain holders to exchange about USD 174 million of the 2028 notes for about USD 120 million of new 10.25% first lien notes of Xerox Corporation and shares equal to 2.93% of those outstanding, cutting principal by up to about USD 54 million and moving USD 120 million of maturities from 2028 to 2030. The exchanged claims would rank ahead of the roughly USD 382 million of 2028 notes left outstanding, and no supplied document confirms that the exchange closed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 42, 56; 10-Q_2026-03-31_xrx-20260331.htm.jsonl, pages 32–33; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 216–217; calculation C14; calculation C18; calculation C19; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation leans on receivable sales and a single supplier, which makes the operating model less self-funding than its recurring revenue suggests. Net cash used in operating activities was USD 77 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 16 million provided a year earlier, with proceeds from sales of finance receivables down from USD 1,102 million in 2023 to USD 357 million in 2025 and USD 122 million in the nine months, and sales that meet certain criteria can force early repayment of first lien debt. Purchases from FUJIFILM Business Innovation, the largest strategic sourcing partner, were USD 811 million in 2025, 11.55% of revenue, and management says it has outsourced a material portion of manufacturing to such partners.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 34, 99; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 20, 28, 129, 205; calculation C21; calculation C22

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious reading is operating and liquidity. Adjusted operating income was USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million on a pro forma basis a year earlier, the adjusted operating margin of 6.6% in the third quarter was 3.3 percentage points higher than a year before, and management states that cash on hand, cash from operations and ABL availability cover at least twelve months of needs without capital markets. The debt-funded buyback is three years old, dividends are being cut and suspended, 2026 repurchases were made at about half of par, and the joint venture raised USD 404 million of net proceeds without issuing common equity.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would turn better if the October 2026 exchange closes on the stated terms, repurchases below par continue, the next annual report names the large holders and an independent board, and the joint venture documents show that existing lenders' collateral did not include the contributed assets. It would turn worse with another transfer of assets into a financing vehicle, more secured debt ahead of the unsecured notes, further purchase accounting corrections, a repeat goodwill impairment, or operating cash flow below the management range of USD 145 million to USD 195 million for 2026, which needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter.

fields.value: - No document after 2026-11-05 is supplied, so the exchange that was expected to close on or about 2026-11-13 is described as expected and the class-specific risk finding may be overstated or understated depending on the final terms and participation.

fields.value: - The quarterly reports now show IT Solutions as its own revenue line while the 2025 annual report split revenue only into equipment sales and post sale revenue, and 2024 revenue lines were recast in that report, so the revenue mix trend mixes two presentations and the shrinking installed base conclusion is stronger on the pro forma growth rates than on the mix shares.

fields.value: - Customer concentration beyond management's statement, renewal rates for managed print services, and the terms of the product supply agreements with FUJIFILM Business Innovation are not disclosed, and the committed obligations disclosed cover only contracts that are not invoiced as rendered, so revenue visibility and supplier dependence are stated qualitatively and the operating model read could be better or worse.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two acquisitions explain most of the change in the structure since 2024. ITsavvy, bought on 2024-11-20, created the IT Solutions segment for USD 404 million, of which USD 194 million was cash and USD 210 million was seller notes due in October 2025 and January 2026. Lexmark, bought from Ninestar Group Company Limited on 2025-07-01, cost USD 768 million at closing including USD 93 million of cash acquired, and USD 749 million after a USD 19 million working capital adjustment finalized in the first quarter of 2026. The 2024 annual report described the pending Lexmark deal as USD 1.5 billion inclusive of net debt and other assumed liabilities, and the bridge from that figure to the equity price is not itemised.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt followed the same path. In March 2024 Holdings issued USD 500 million of notes due 2029 and USD 400 million of 3.75% convertible notes due 2030. In April and May 2025 Xerox Corporation issued USD 400 million of 10.25% first lien notes due 2030 at 99% of par and USD 500 million of 13.5% second lien notes due 2031 at 98% and 95% of par, and about USD 494 million of escrowed second lien proceeds was released at the Lexmark closing. On 2025-07-01 Holdings issued USD 125 million of 13.00% unsecured notes due June 2026 and USD 250 million of 13.00% notes due 2030 with a pre-funded warrant, and Xerox Corporation borrowed USD 327 million of incremental first lien term loans. In 2025 Xerox received about USD 375 million from issuing senior notes and about USD 904 million from secured debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The February 2026 joint venture is the largest new financing since the 2025 annual report. Xerox Corporation contributed the Xerox brand trademarks and related intellectual property to XRX Brandco Holdings LLC for Class B units, and investors funded USD 405 million of five-year senior secured term loans and USD 45 million of Class A units, which carry a mandatory cumulative redemption in five years unless the holders defer it. The proceeds were distributed to Xerox Corporation for general corporate purposes and for opportunistic work on the capital structure, including debt repayment. The 2025 annual report states USD 42 million of fees, while the third quarter report states USD 46 million paid at closing and USD 8 million later.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Equity-linked and liability management steps followed in 2026. Holders of common stock, Series A preferred stock and the convertible notes received warrants to buy shares at USD 8.00 each for cash or with designated notes, over a number of shares equal to 58.01% of those outstanding, and 1.36% of the warrants had been exercised by 2026-09-30, one exercise retiring about USD 8 million of the convertible notes. The company also repurchased USD 194 million of the 2028 notes and USD 6 million of the 2031 second lien notes, and sold rights to USD 105 million of tariff refund receivables for about USD 80 million of cash, a discount of USD 25 million, which is shown in financing activities with a USD 81 million liability outside total debt at 2026-09-30.

No supplied document confirms the exchange closed.

fields.value: The proxy statement that holds beneficial ownership, board membership, executive compensation and related-party items is not supplied, so who controls the vote, whether the Icahn parties still hold shares and whether insider arrangements exist cannot be established. This limits the ownership picture and the governance risk level to issuer behaviour. Severity: Material. Action: obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The executed joint venture credit agreement, the licence agreement and guarantee, the indentures and the intercreditor agreements are not supplied, so whether the contributed brand assets were collateral for earlier notes, and how much room remains for further secured debt, cannot be tested. Severity: Material. Action: obtain the agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The levels of the asset coverage ratio and the minimum revenue covenants in the joint venture documents are not stated, so headroom against a default or a call for extra support from Xerox cannot be measured. Severity: Material. Action: obtain the joint venture agreements and any compliance certificates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No document after 2026-11-05 is supplied, so the closing and final terms of the 2028 notes exchange, the participants in it and whether it was open to all holders are not established. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain the next quarterly report or a current report on the closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The terms of Amendment No. 2 to the first lien term loan agreement, filed by reference to a current report dated 2026-10-29, are not stated in the supplied reports, so any change to baskets or covenants ahead of the exchange is not established. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain the amendment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Customer concentration beyond management's statement, renewal rates for managed print services and the terms of the supply agreements with FUJIFILM Business Innovation are not disclosed, so revenue visibility and supplier dependence are stated qualitatively. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain management disclosure and the supply agreements.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The holder of the Series A preferred stock, the notes designated for warrant exercise and the rating agency and rating level are not named in the supplied filings, so the vote held by the preferred stock, the route for exchanging debt for equity and rating-linked terms cannot be assessed. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain the proxy statement, the warrant agreement and rating reports.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The filings state different figures for the ITsavvy price, the Lexmark headline and equity price, the joint venture fees, the issuer of the 13.00% notes due 2030 and the synergy target; each is shown in the conflict log with its sources and none is reconciled beyond the choice stated there. Severity: Minor. Action: none needed for this snapshot unless the Lexmark headline size matters, in which case obtain the purchase agreement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit for Xerox Holdings Corp (issuer xrx-1770450), as of 2026-11-18, on the credit snapshot pathway. The scope is the overall fundamental credit profile of the issuer, its strongest support, its weakest dimension and its primary downside path, drawn from the five supplied filings and the earlier module findings. Security selection, legal capacity, recovery and portfolio sizing are outside this scope.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox is a weak credit: a shrinking print business carrying total debt of USD 4,220 million with negative reported EBITDA, negative book equity and USD 1,889 million due in 2028 and 2029, so creditors rely on cost savings, receivable sales and refinancing access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 4–5, 100–101; calculation C1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity covers the next twelve months on management's account and adjusted earnings are recovering, so a default before 2028 is not the central risk. The central risk is a further fall in operating cash flow that leaves the 2028 and 2029 maturities to be refinanced at coupons above 10%, with a growing share of debt secured ahead of the unsecured notes. Governance risk is medium.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 95, 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 218–219; calculation C18; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business risk is weak because a mostly recurring revenue base is shrinking. Post sale revenue was 79% of FY2025 revenue and committed multi-year service obligations were USD 636 million at 2026-09-30, but on a pro forma basis revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in the first nine months of 2026, and the IT Solutions line fell 12.1%. Equipment installations rose 9.0% in the third quarter of 2026 and the pro forma decline narrowed from the second quarter, which is a first sign of stabilisation rather than a trend.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high and has fallen only because earnings recovered, not because debt fell. Net debt of USD 3,808 million at 2026-09-30 is USD 3,754 million pro forma for the exchange of 2028 notes expected on 2026-11-13, and pro forma net leverage is not established. Net debt is 4.46x house-adjusted EBITDA of USD 854 million for the last twelve months against 6.42x at FY2025, a fall of 1.96x in which net debt rose USD 73 million and EBITDA rose 46.74%. Reported EBITDA is negative USD 275 million for the same twelve months after the USD 959 million goodwill impairment, the issuer states no EBITDA, and its own target of total debt below 3.0x EBITDA compares with 4.94x on the house measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation C7; calculation C19

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest absorbs a growing share of earnings, so coverage is thin and falling. Adjusted operating income plus depreciation covered non-financing interest expense 2.18x over the last twelve months against 4.23x in FY2024, because non-financing interest expense rose 64.88% in the first nine months of 2026 and total interest expense rose 41.45%, on higher rates on the Lexmark borrowings and the brand financing, and the 2025 secured issues carry coupons of 10.25% and 13.5%. The 13.00% notes due 2030 step up toward 16.75% by July 2030, and reported EBITDA covered FY2025 cash interest only 0.65x; cash interest is not printed for the 2026 interim periods.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 96, 219–220, 227; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C2; calculation C3; calculation C18; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash generation is the weakest dimension. Net cash used in operating activities was USD 77 million in the first nine months of 2026, free cash flow for the last twelve months was USD 37 million, or 4.33% of house-adjusted EBITDA against 76.68% in FY2024, and management cut its 2026 operating cash flow guidance to USD 145 million to USD 195 million from about USD 340 million on lower profitability, lower proceeds from sales of finance receivables and lower collections of tariff refunds. The range needs USD 222 million to USD 272 million in the fourth quarter against USD 208 million in the fourth quarter of 2025, and a repeat of last year's quarter would leave the year at USD 131 million, below the range.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 97; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 71; calculation C4; calculation C5; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate to the end of 2027 but the refinancing wall behind it is large. Cash of USD 412 million and net ABL availability of about USD 225 million cover the USD 217 million of principal due to the end of 2027 by 2.94x, and management says liquidity is sufficient for at least twelve months, but principal due is USD 752 million in 2028, USD 1,137 million in 2029 and USD 1,042 million in 2030, USD 2,931 million in all, and the ABL matures in May 2028. Pro forma cash for the exchange is not established, because accrued interest on the exchanged notes is paid in cash and not stated. Management expects to address the maturities through cash from operations, refinancings and liability management whose timing and terms are uncertain.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 42, 56, 95, 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Creditors are increasingly ranked by security and by entity, which raises class-specific risk for unsecured holders. About 47.15% of principal debt is now secured, USD 451 million sits in subsidiaries below Xerox Corporation, USD 450 million of it the brand financing, and the exchange would add about USD 120 million of first lien notes, while management states that further transactions may be pari passu with or effectively senior to existing debt. The company's own estimate puts the fair value of Holdings long-term debt at 49.10% of carrying amount against 76.02% for Xerox Corporation, which is an estimate and not a traded price.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 46–47, 56, 98–99, 101; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 216–217; calculation C9; calculation C8

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy is moving toward creditors but equity no longer protects them, and governance risk is medium. Dividends on common and preferred stock are suspended from January 2027, USD 200 million of notes were bought back at 50.50% of principal and capital expenditure is 1.23% of revenue, yet Holdings reports a shareholders' deficit of USD 683 million and ownership, board and related-party disclosure sits in a proxy statement that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 40, 56; calculation C11; calculation C17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weak reading is that earnings have turned. Adjusted operating income was USD 399 million in the first nine months of 2026 against USD 243 million on a pro forma basis a year earlier, house-adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 854 million for the last twelve months from USD 582 million in FY2025, the issuer targets more than USD 300 million of synergies by the end of 2027 and cumulative run-rate gross savings already exceed USD 500 million. The company has also retired debt at about half of par, raised USD 404 million of net proceeds from the brand financing without issuing common equity, and suspended dividends, so it has shown that it can create liquidity when it needs to.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 40, 112; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if the fourth quarter delivers the USD 222 million to USD 272 million of operating cash flow that the guidance implies, the exchange closes on the stated terms, the 2028 maturities are refinanced before they become current, and the next proxy statement shows a settled ownership and board. It would worsen with fourth quarter operating cash flow below USD 208 million, further asset-backed or secured financings or exchanges that move claims ahead of the unsecured notes, ABL borrowings rising above USD 75 million, or another goodwill impairment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - The issuer states no EBITDA and prints no cash interest for 2026 interim periods, so the conclusion that leverage is high and coverage thin rests on analyst-built measures, and a different add-back set or the actual cash interest could move both ratios either way.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - No agency rating, bond price or spread is supplied and the debt fair values are the company's own estimates, so the finding that creditors are ranked by security rests on structure and company estimates, and market pricing could show a different spread between the classes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Management's only forward figure is the 2026 operating cash flow range, so the outlook and the downside scenario are built from reported trends and are qualitative, and a harsher or milder path than described cannot be ruled out.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Covenant definitions, the springing ABL test levels and the secured debt capacity are known only from filing summaries, so headroom is not measured and the conclusion that liquidity is adequate to 2027 could change if a covenant restricts borrowing earlier than assumed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox sells print equipment, supplies, managed print and digital services and lease financing through Print and Other, which was 89% of FY2025 revenue, and integrated IT infrastructure services through IT Solutions, which was 11%. The business earned revenue of USD 7,022 million in FY2025 with a workforce of about twenty-three thousand, 43.25% of revenue outside the United States, and no single customer or small group of customers on which management says it depends. Lexmark, bought on 2025-07-01, added USD 962 million of 2025 revenue, and ITsavvy, bought in 2024, created the IT Solutions segment.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The model supports cash flow visibility through the recurring post sale base and committed multi-year obligations of USD 636 million, but the base is tied to an installed base that is shrinking and the finance arm needs USD 1,296 million of allocated debt and regular receivable sales, so the model supports debt service less than its recurring revenue suggests and makes refinancing confidence depend on cost savings rather than growth.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19, 100; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Xerox Holdings is a listed parent with no financial sponsor or controlling holder named, and Xerox Corporation, wholly owned, holds nearly all operations. The parent carries USD 1,698 million of principal debt guaranteed by Xerox Corporation, Xerox Corporation carries USD 2,199 million, much of it secured, and subsidiaries below it carry USD 451 million, USD 450 million of it the brand financing, so unsecured parent debt is structurally behind secured and subsidiary debt except through the guarantees.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy has been mixed: a debt-funded repurchase in 2023 was followed by dividend cuts in 2025, a suspension from January 2027 and discounted repurchases of notes in 2026, while a brand financing, a warrant distribution and a pending exchange show a willingness to restructure claims. Governance risk is medium because behaviour is supportive in cash terms but ownership and board control are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is recurring in form but declining in volume. Post sale revenue, which includes supplies, service, rentals, financing and IT products, was 79% of FY2025 revenue, committed multi-year obligations were USD 636 million, and no single customer is said to matter, yet pro forma revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in nine months 2026 on lower equipment service, managed print, supplies and rental revenue, and renewal rates are not disclosed. IT Solutions fell 18.9% in the third quarter on the timing of large public sector placements, so it adds diversification but not yet stability. Pricing actions have offset part of tariff costs, but supplier cost increases may not be passed on to customers.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit implication is that revenue visibility supports debt service for the next one to five years of committed contracts but not the 2028 to 2030 refinancing window, because lower page volumes, reduced print usage and customer non-renewal are the mechanisms through which cash flow before interest shrinks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are being rebuilt by cost action rather than pricing power. Total gross margin was 27.1% in FY2025 against 31.5% in FY2024, adjusted operating margin was 3.5% in FY2025 and 6.6% in the third quarter of 2026, and run-rate gross savings above USD 500 million were achieved through 2025 with more than USD 300 million of synergies targeted by the end of 2027. Fixed commitments limit flexibility, since outsourced shared services and technology commitments total USD 1,000 million, and purchases from FUJIFILM Business Innovation, a supplier that is also a listed competitor, were 11.55% of revenue, with memory price increases and tariffs adding input cost.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7, 89–90, 129–130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 13, 59–60; calculation C16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins can be defended against modest volume pressure through further cost action, but operating leverage is negative and a further 5.0% revenue fall at the last twelve months' margins would remove about USD 118 million of gross profit, 23.55% of last twelve months' adjusted operating income, which is an arithmetic illustration and not a forecast.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low, at 1.30% of revenue in FY2025, so capital expenditure offers little further room to cut. Free cash flow fell from USD 467 million in FY2024 to USD 133 million in FY2025 and USD 37 million for the last twelve months because operating cash flow fell with lower receivable sales, restructuring payments, pension contributions of USD 118 million in nine months 2026 and cash interest of USD 272 million in FY2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 227; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 47; calculation C11; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: EBITDA therefore does not translate into durable free cash flow today: conversion fell from 76.68% to 4.33% of house-adjusted EBITDA, which leaves little for debt reduction except asset-backed funding, so the maturity wall depends on earnings growth and market access.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Rivalry is intense: Brother, Canon, FUJIFILM Business Innovation, HP, Konica Minolta, Kyocera and Ricoh compete in print on price, technology and service, and no market share data are supplied, so price pressure and equipment placement losses reduce post sale revenue and the cash that supports debt. The filings do not discuss new entrants, so that force is not assessed. Substitutes matter because the annual report lists customers selecting alternative technologies and reduced print usage among the factors that can end or shrink contracts, and lower page volumes are cited in the revenue decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Buyers include commercial clients and government entities whose agreements are generally renewable at the customer's option or cancellable, so buyer power limits pricing, and supplier power is high because FUJIFILM Business Innovation, a competitor, also supplies products, parts and supplies and purchases from it were USD 811 million in 2025, which exposes gross margin to supplier terms.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Policy and macro factors are material to credit. Tariffs raised costs in 2025 and refunds of tariffs paid became estimable in 2026, which the company sold for about USD 80 million of cash against USD 105 million of receivables, memory price increases and macro uncertainty led to the USD 959 million impairment, the joint venture loans link interest cost to the reference rate, and 43.25% of revenue is outside the United States. Social and technological factors matter because the annual report lists reduced print usage and customers selecting alternative technologies among the reasons contracts end or shrink, and lower page volumes are cited in the revenue decline.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths are a recurring post sale base, a diversified customer base, low capital intensity and a cost programme that has lifted adjusted operating income. Weaknesses are a shrinking installed base, thin interest coverage, weak cash generation and negative equity. Opportunities that could improve credit quality are synergy delivery above USD 300 million, growth in IT and digital services, and discounted debt retirement. Threats that could weaken it are the 2028 to 2030 maturities, further priming of unsecured claims, supplier and tariff costs, and further goodwill impairments.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first strength is a recurring, geographically diversified revenue base with no stated customer concentration, because post sale revenue is 79% of FY2025 revenue and committed obligations are USD 636 million, which gives cash flow visibility that supports debt service through 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second strength is a cost-led earnings recovery, because adjusted operating income rose to USD 399 million from USD 243 million pro forma and the issuer targets more than USD 300 million of synergies by the end of 2027, which lowers leverage if it is delivered.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 112; 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 7; calculation C20

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third strength is liquidity and financial policy that protect the next two years, because cash of USD 412 million and net ABL availability of about USD 225 million cover principal due to the end of 2027 by 2.94x, dividends are suspended and debt was bought back at 50.50% of principal; pro forma cash for the exchange of 2028 notes expected on 2026-11-13 is not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 40, 42, 56; calculation C12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth strength is low capital intensity at 1.23% of revenue, which keeps capital spending from consuming cash, although it also leaves little room to cut.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first weakness is a shrinking base, because pro forma revenue fell 7.6% in 2025 and 5.0% in nine months 2026, which reduces the cash flow before interest that supports the debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The second weakness is weak cash generation, because operating cash flow was negative USD 77 million in nine months 2026 and free cash flow was 4.33% of house-adjusted EBITDA, which leaves refinancing and asset-backed funding to meet maturities.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 97; calculation C4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The third weakness is a thin and falling interest cover of 2.18x on adjusted operating income plus depreciation, because higher rates on acquisition borrowings and the brand financing raised non-financing interest expense by 64.88% in nine months 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 43; calculation C2; calculation C3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fourth weakness is a maturity wall and eroding priority, because USD 2,931 million falls due in 2028 to 2030, 47.15% of principal debt is secured and the exchange and brand financing move claims ahead of unsecured notes, which raises class-specific risk.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 56, 99–101; calculation C1; calculation C9

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fifth weakness is negative equity and unsettled governance, because Holdings reports a deficit of USD 683 million and ownership and board disclosure is not supplied, which removes a book cushion and leaves sponsor support unassessable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit supports are a recurring revenue base, low capital intensity, a cost programme and liquidity to the end of 2027; the constraints are high leverage, thin cover, weak cash generation, maturities concentrated in 2028 to 2030 and negative equity. The trend is improving in earnings, as net leverage on house-adjusted EBITDA fell 1.96x in nine months (pro forma net leverage for the exchange expected on 2026-11-13 is not established), but worsening in cash flow, as operating cash flow turned negative and guidance was cut by half at the midpoint, so the two trends diverge and the earnings gain has not yet reached cash.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 97; calculation C7; calculation C6

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Claims outside the debt figure add to the burden: balance sheet liabilities for pensions and retiree medical of USD 1,135 million equal 26.90% of total debt, and outsourced shared services and technology commitments are USD 1,000 million, so fixed claims on cash are larger than the debt table shows.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Business & governance (CP-1A); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 129–130; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation C13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The missing datapoints are an issuer-stated EBITDA, interim cash interest, agency ratings and market prices, executed covenant documents and the identity of controlling holders, which limit how firmly the profile can be rated.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In the next twelve to 24 months the supports are the synergy programme, a fourth quarter operating cash flow of USD 222 million to USD 272 million, the exchange of 2028 notes, dividend suspension and USD 217 million of principal due to the end of 2027; the pressures are falling finance receivable sales, memory price increases and further tariff effects. Over three to five years the first lien term loan amortizes at 7.50% a year in 2026 and 10% a year after, the joint venture amortizes USD 81 million a year, the 13.00% notes due 2030 step up toward 16.75%, and USD 2,931 million falls due in 2028 to 2030, so cash must rise materially or refinancing must succeed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 219–220, 223; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 39, 59, 97, 100–101; calculation C1; calculation C5; calculation C14

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sector tailwinds the issuer cites are client demand for integrated infrastructure, cloud, security and automation services and the footprint and A4 colour and Asia Pacific reach that Lexmark adds; the sector headwinds are lower page volumes, memory price increases and tariffs. Company tailwinds are cost savings and tariff refunds; company headwinds are leverage, refinancing and the loss of receivable sale proceeds.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The realistic downside, an analyst scenario and not a management projection, begins with continued mid single digit revenue decline, a fall in sales of finance receivables and slower cost savings. Revenue falling another 5.0% at current margins would remove about USD 118 million of gross profit, which is 23.55% of adjusted operating income, and a fourth quarter that repeats last year would leave 2026 operating cash flow at USD 131 million, below management's range. Free cash flow would stay near zero after restructuring, pension and interest payments, so cash and the ABL would be drawn, and the borrowing base would fall if receivables and inventory fell.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); 10-K_2025-12-31_xrx-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 224; 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5, 42, 97; calculation C10; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The first operational break would be the 2027 and 2028 cash needs rather than a payment default: principal due is USD 217 million to the end of 2027, then USD 752 million in 2028, with the ABL maturing in May 2028. Management levers are further asset sales, more asset-backed financing and liability management, each of which would move claims ahead of unsecured holders, while capital expenditure and dividends are already low. Resilience looks sufficient to avoid liquidity distress through 2027 on management's statement but not sufficient to refinance 2028 and 2029 without further priming; the observable triggers are fourth quarter operating cash flow, ABL borrowings, the closing of the exchange and any new secured issue.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Xerox presents a weak business profile supported by a recurring revenue base, a cost programme and liquidity to the end of 2027, but credit quality is constrained by high leverage, thin interest cover, weak cash generation and negative equity. Cash-flow durability appears weak because operating cash flow turned negative and guidance was cut. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on delivery of the cost programme, receivable sales and the willingness of lenders to accept more secured debt. The primary downside path is falling operating cash flow ahead of the 2028 and 2029 maturities. Further analysis would require an issuer-stated EBITDA, interim cash interest, ratings and prices and the executed debt documents. Top risk: refinancing the 2028 and 2029 maturities on falling operating cash flow.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); Source readiness (CP-0); 10-Q_2026-09-30_xrx-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 95–97; calculation C1; calculation C5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The registers below are complete and unabridged, one under each heading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Each calculation uses only figures printed in the supplied filings or stated in this answer's tables or the earlier module findings; negative amounts carry a minus sign.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer states no EBITDA and prints no cash interest for the 2026 interim periods, so leverage and coverage rest on analyst-built measures and on non-financing interest expense as a proxy for cash interest. Severity: Material. Action: obtain the issuer's own EBITDA definition and the interim cash flow supplement.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The executed ABL, term loan, indenture and intercreditor documents are not supplied, so covenant levels, the springing test, the secured debt limit and the room for further priming are known only from filing summaries and headroom is not measured. Severity: Material. Action: obtain the agreements and any compliance certificates.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No agency rating, bond price or yield is supplied, so market pricing of the classes and any rating-linked terms are not established. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain rating reports and bond prices.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The exchange of 2028 notes was expected on or about 2026-11-13 and no document after 2026-11-05 is supplied, so its closing and final terms are not established and pro forma net leverage and cash are not established. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain the next quarterly report or the current report on the closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management gives one forward figure, the 2026 operating cash flow range, and no revenue, margin, capital expenditure or leverage outlook, so the outlook and downside scenario are qualitative. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain management's targets at the next earnings update.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The proxy statement holding ownership, board and related-party disclosure is not supplied, so who controls the vote and whether insider arrangements exist is not established and governance risk rests on issuer behaviour. Severity: Minor. Action: obtain the 2026 proxy statement.

fields.value: The orchestrator selects the next module.
